words.enDefinition: so good or special that people remember it

examples.en: The welcome dinner my host family cooked was truly memorable.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭做的欢迎晚宴真是一段「难忘」的经历。

examples.en: Her graduation speech was so memorable that people still quote it now.
examples.zh: 她的毕业演讲「令人难忘」，到现在还有人引用里面的话。

words.enDefinition: impossible to forget because it is so special

examples.en: Studying abroad gave me unforgettable memories of late-night talks with my roommates.
examples.zh: 留学让我收获了和室友深夜长谈这段「难以忘怀」的回忆。

examples.en: The sunrise from the mountaintop after that overnight hike was absolutely unforgettable.
examples.zh: 那次通宵徒步后山顶的日出，美得「难以忘怀」。

words.enDefinition: not special enough for anyone to remember it

examples.en: The movie had great special effects, but the plot itself was completely forgettable.
examples.zh: 这部电影特效不错，但剧情本身「看过就忘」。

examples.en: His first stand-up set was so forgettable that I can't recall a single joke.
examples.zh: 他的脱口秀首秀平淡得让人「看过就忘」，我一个段子都想不起来。

words.enDefinition: not as good as many people claim

examples.en: Honestly, that cafe near campus is overrated—the coffee is just average.
examples.zh: 说实话，学校附近那家咖啡店「被高估」了，咖啡就是普通水平。

examples.en: Some classmates call that major overrated, but I still find its courses useful.
examples.zh: 有些同学说这个专业「名过其实」，但我还是觉得课程挺有用。

words.enDefinition: better or more important than people realize

examples.en: The library basement is an underrated study spot—quiet, warm, and rarely full.
examples.zh: 图书馆地下室是个「被低估」的自习好去处，安静、暖和还几乎不挤。

examples.en: That tiny noodle shop is seriously underrated; their broth beats the famous chains.
examples.zh: 那家小面馆真的「被低估」了，汤底比连锁名店还好。

words.enDefinition: less impressive than you expected or hoped

examples.en: The trailer looked amazing, but the film itself turned out pretty underwhelming.
examples.zh: 预告片看着很燃，正片却相当「平平无奇」。

examples.en: His first draft was underwhelming, so the professor asked for stronger evidence.
examples.zh: 他的初稿写得「平平无奇」，教授要求补充更有力的论据。

words.enDefinition: of the highest quality or standard

examples.en: The campus gym has top-notch equipment, so I squeeze in workouts between classes.
examples.zh: 学校健身房器械「一流」，我就趁课间去练一会儿。

examples.en: Her presentation was top-notch, and the recruiter invited her back for a second round.
examples.zh: 她的展示堪称「一流」，招聘官直接请她进入二面。

words.enDefinition: below the usual expected standard

examples.en: The Wi-Fi in my dorm is subpar, so I do my uploads in the library.
examples.zh: 宿舍的Wi-Fi「不达标」，要传文件我都去图书馆。

examples.en: Customer service at that phone company was subpar when I tried to cancel my plan.
examples.zh: 我去那家运营商取消套餐，客服服务实在「不达标」。

words.enDefinition: only average and not very good

examples.en: His grades were mediocre last term, so he cut gaming hours to focus.
examples.zh: 他上学期成绩「平庸」，于是减少了打游戏的时间。

examples.en: The restaurant had mediocre reviews, so our group booked somewhere else for dinner.
examples.zh: 那家餐厅评价「平平」，我们聚餐就订了别家。

words.enDefinition: lower in quality or status than another

examples.en: He assumed the off-brand laptop was inferior, but it handled all his coursework fine.
examples.zh: 他以为杂牌笔记本「质量较差」，结果完成所有课业毫无压力。

examples.en: Stop comparing yourself—being on a different timeline doesn't make you inferior.
examples.zh: 别老跟人比，节奏不同不代表你就「低人一等」。

words.enDefinition: unusually good and standing out

examples.en: She made exceptional progress in academic writing after one semester in the language program.
examples.zh: 在语言项目读了一个学期，她的学术写作进步「格外出色」。

examples.en: The professor praised my group's exceptional field research on campus recycling.
examples.zh: 教授称赞我们小组关于校园回收的实地调研「格外出色」。

words.enDefinition: very noticeable and catching attention at once

examples.en: The photo exhibit shows a striking contrast between campus life in 1990 and today.
examples.zh: 摄影展里1990年与如今的校园生活形成「引人注目」的对比。

examples.en: Her striking red coat made her easy to spot in the crowded station.
examples.zh: 她那件「引人注目」的红大衣让我在拥挤的车站一眼认出她。

words.enDefinition: so beautiful that it astonishes you

examples.en: The view from the library rooftop at sunset is absolutely breathtaking.
examples.zh: 日落时图书馆天台的景色「美得惊人」。

examples.en: We hiked three hours uphill, but the breathtaking scenery repaid every step.
examples.zh: 我们爬了三小时山路，但那「美得惊人」的风景让每一步都值了。

words.enDefinition: extremely beautiful or impressively attractive

examples.en: My roommate looked stunning in her dress at the international culture night.
examples.zh: 国际文化之夜上，室友的礼服造型十分「惊艳」。

examples.en: The wedding photos came out stunning even though it rained all morning.
examples.zh: 虽然下了一上午的雨，婚纱照还是拍得「惊艳」。

words.enDefinition: so valuable that no money can replace it

examples.en: The old photos of my grandparents are priceless, so I back them up in two places.
examples.zh: 祖父母的旧照片「无价」，我存在两个地方做备份。

examples.en: Her advice about internship applications was priceless when I started job hunting.
examples.zh: 我开始找工作时，她给的实习申请建议简直「无价」。

words.enDefinition: deserving the time or effort you put in

examples.en: The volunteer program was worthwhile because I made friends and improved my English.
examples.zh: 这个志愿项目很「值得」，我既交了朋友又练了英语。

examples.en: Flying home for one weekend is expensive, but for my sister's wedding it felt worthwhile.
examples.zh: 为一个周末飞回家不便宜，但赶上姐姐的婚礼就觉得「值」。

words.enDefinition: not able to do anything helpful

examples.en: The old printer in the study room is useless—it jams on every third page.
examples.zh: 自习室那台旧打印机「没用」，每打三页卡一次。

examples.en: I felt useless in the group project until someone finally shared the folder with me.
examples.zh: 没人给我共享文件夹之前，我在小组作业里感觉特别「没用」。

words.enDefinition: doomed to fail, so not worth doing

examples.en: Arguing with the automated phone menu felt futile, so I went to the branch in person.
examples.zh: 跟语音电话菜单争论纯属「徒劳」，我干脆直接去了网点。

examples.en: It's futile to memorize vocabulary if you never use it in real conversations.
examples.zh: 背了单词从不在对话里用，这样的努力就是「徒劳」。

words.enDefinition: having no purpose, value, or sense

examples.en: Without real examples, those grammar rules felt completely meaningless to me.
examples.zh: 缺了真实例句，那些语法规则显得「无意义」。

examples.en: He quit chasing likes online because the numbers felt meaningless without real friendships.
examples.zh: 他不再追着点赞跑，因为缺了真实的友谊，那些数字「毫无意义」。

words.enDefinition: giving you satisfaction and purpose

examples.en: Tutoring middle schoolers on weekends is tiring but genuinely fulfilling.
examples.zh: 周末给初中生做辅导很累，但真的「有成就感」。

examples.en: She switched majors after two semesters because accounting felt efficient but never fulfilling.
examples.zh: 读了两个学期后她转了专业，会计虽然吃香却让她毫无「成就感」。

words.enDefinition: making you feel pleased and content

examples.en: There's something deeply satisfying about folding warm laundry straight from the dryer.
examples.zh: 把刚烘干的衣服叠好，有种说不出的「畅快」。

examples.en: Crossing the finish line of my first 10K was the most satisfying moment this year.
examples.zh: 完成人生第一个十公里的冲线时刻，是今年最「令人畅快」的一刻。

words.enDefinition: full of interesting or exciting things happening

examples.en: It was an eventful first week—lost luggage, a snowstorm, and three new friends.
examples.zh: 开学第一周真是「波澜起伏」：行李丢了、遇上涨雪，还交了三个新朋友。

examples.en: Our road trip was eventful enough to fill the group chat for a month.
examples.zh: 这趟自驾游「波折不断」，够群里聊一个月了。

words.enDefinition: well known for something bad

examples.en: That intersection near campus is notorious for fender benders, so I cross carefully.
examples.zh: 校门口那个路口「出了名」地爱追尾，我过马路格外小心。

examples.en: Our building's elevator is notorious for breaking down right before morning classes.
examples.zh: 我们楼的电梯「出了名地差劲」，总在早课前罢工。

words.enDefinition: very famous and admired for a long time

examples.en: The all-night diner near campus is legendary among students cramming for finals.
examples.zh: 校外那家通宵餐馆在赶期末的学生中堪称「传奇」。

examples.en: Grandma's dumpling recipe is legendary in our family, and nobody has the full version.
examples.zh: 奶奶的饺子配方是我们家的「传奇」，没人拿到完整版。

words.enDefinition: famous and widely seen as a symbol of something

examples.en: Taking a photo under the iconic clock tower is on every freshman's checklist.
examples.zh: 在「标志性」的钟楼下打卡拍照，是每个新生的清单项目。

examples.en: That cafe's iconic neon sign has welcomed students to Main Street for fifty years.
examples.zh: 那家咖啡馆「标志性的」霓虹招牌已经在主街迎了五十年学生。

words.enDefinition: extremely good, clever, or impressive

examples.en: Splitting the bulk groceries three ways was a brilliant idea that saved everyone money.
examples.zh: 三个人分摊大包装采购真是个「绝妙」的主意，人人都省了钱。

examples.en: Her brilliant shared spreadsheet finally ended our roommates' fights over the kitchen.
examples.zh: 她那份「绝妙的」共享表格终于终结了室友间的厨房大战。

words.enDefinition: extremely good or impressive in an exciting way

examples.en: The advisor was awesome about rescheduling my placement test around my work shift.
examples.zh: 顾问「极棒」，把我的分级考试安排在了下班之后。

examples.en: Your slides look awesome—did you really make that animated chart yourself?
examples.zh: 你的幻灯片「超棒」——那个动态图表真是你自己做的？

words.enDefinition: making you believe that something is true

examples.en: Her argument for keeping the writing center open was convincing, and the dean listened.
examples.zh: 她主张保留写作中心的理由「令人信服」，院长听了进去。

examples.en: His excuse for missing practice sounded convincing, but the coach still checked the schedule.
examples.zh: 他缺训的借口听着「可信」，教练还是去核了课表。

words.enDefinition: good at making people agree or act

examples.en: Our persuasive poster campaign convinced the student council to fund the rooftop garden.
examples.zh: 我们「有说服力」的海报攻势让学生会批准了天台花园的经费。

examples.en: Writing persuasive essays got easier once I learned to answer the other side's points first.
examples.zh: 学会先回应对方观点之后，写「有说服力的」议论文就容易多了。

words.enDefinition: seeming reasonable or likely to be true

examples.en: His explanation for the lost package sounded plausible, so I waited one more week.
examples.zh: 他对包裹丢失的解释听着「合理」，我就又等了一周。

examples.en: The tutor offered a plausible reason for the calculus error and walked me through the fix.
examples.zh: 助教对微积分错误给出了「说得通」的解释，还带我一步步改正。

words.enDefinition: giving a false or incomplete impression

examples.en: The apartment listing was misleading—that 'spacious bedroom' barely fit a desk and bed.
examples.zh: 那条租房信息「有误导性」——所谓宽敞卧室连一张书桌加床都勉强。

examples.en: My professor warned us that secondhand summaries can be misleading when citing research.
examples.zh: 教授提醒我们，引用研究时看二手总结容易被「误导」。

words.enDefinition: made to seem larger or better than reality

examples.en: His story about the blizzard was slightly exaggerated, though the roads truly were terrible.
examples.zh: 他讲暴风雪的经历略有「夸张」，不过路况当时确实糟糕。

examples.en: Online reviews here tend to be exaggerated, so I test products before judging them.
examples.zh: 这里的网评往往「夸大其词」，所以我先试用再下判断。

words.enDefinition: pretending to have beliefs you do not follow

examples.en: Banning phones while texting through the whole meeting felt hypocritical to the club.
examples.zh: 自己开会全程刷手机却禁止大家用手机，社员们觉得这很「虚伪」。

examples.en: She called it hypocritical to hold wellness week with three exams back to back.
examples.zh: 一边办身心健康周一边连排三场考试，她说这太「虚伪」了。

words.enDefinition: probably not honest, good, or reliable

examples.en: The secondhand seller's answer about the cracked screen was questionable, so I walked away.
examples.zh: 二手卖家对屏幕裂缝的解释「有问题」，我扭头就走。

examples.en: His claim that the deposit was nonrefundable seemed questionable, so we reread the lease.
examples.zh: 他说押金一律不退，这点「存疑」，我们又把租约读了一遍。

words.enDefinition: not likely to happen or succeed

examples.en: It's doubtful the campus shuttle will run on time during the snowstorm, so leave early.
examples.zh: 暴雪天校车能不能准点「很难说」，你最好早点出门。

examples.en: I'm doubtful the landlord will fix the heater before December, so I emailed him again today.
examples.zh: 房东十二月前修不修暖气我很「怀疑」，今天又给他发了邮件。

words.enDefinition: open to argument and reasonable disagreement

examples.en: Whether a gap year helps your career is debatable, so I asked several alumni first.
examples.zh: 间隔年对职业有没有帮助「见仁见智」，我先问了几位学长学姐。

examples.en: It's debatable which library floor is quietest, but the top one wins for most people.
examples.zh: 图书馆哪层最安静「说法不一」，不过多数人投顶楼。

words.enDefinition: considering only one person's view or interest

examples.en: The article on the tuition hike felt one-sided because it never quoted a single student.
examples.zh: 那篇学费上涨的报道很「片面」，从头到尾没采访一个学生。

examples.en: Their friendship became one-sided—she always made the plans and covered the rideshare.
examples.zh: 她们的友谊变得「一边倒」，永远是她安排行程、她付车费。

words.enDefinition: unfairly favoring one side or group

examples.en: He worried the peer evaluation was biased because his partner disliked group debates.
examples.zh: 他担心同伴互评「不客观」，因为搭档本来就讨厌小组辩论。

examples.en: A biased sample ruined our first survey, so we collected responses outside that one dorm.
examples.zh: 第一份问卷因样本「有偏」而废掉，后来我们走出那栋楼去收数据。

words.enDefinition: not supporting any side in a disagreement

examples.en: I stayed neutral all winter while my roommates fought over the thermostat setting.
examples.zh: 室友俩为空调温度争了一整个冬天，我始终保持「中立」。

examples.en: The moderator kept a neutral tone while the candidates argued about parking fees.
examples.zh: 候选人争论停车费时，主持人始终保持「中立」语气。

words.enDefinition: based on personal feelings rather than facts

examples.en: Taste in music is totally subjective, so we stopped arguing about each other's playlists.
examples.zh: 音乐品味完全是「主观」的，我们就不互相吐槽歌单了。

examples.en: Grading art projects is subjective, which is why the professor shares a detailed rubric.
examples.zh: 艺术作业打分很「主观」，所以教授公布了详细的评分标准。

words.enDefinition: hard to believe because too unlikely

examples.en: His excuse that a raccoon ate his homework sounded far-fetched even to the tutor.
examples.zh: 他的借口——作业被浣熊吃了——实在「牵强」，连助教都不信。

examples.en: The movie's plot was so far-fetched that we couldn't take the villain seriously.
examples.zh: 电影情节「太过牵强」，反派都显得毫无威慑力。

words.enDefinition: not sensible or possible in real life

examples.en: Joining five study groups every week was unrealistic once midterms actually started.
examples.zh: 期中一开始，每周参加五个学习小组就成了「不现实」的想法。

examples.en: The landlord's strict no-guests rule felt unrealistic for students whose families visit from abroad.
examples.zh: 房东不许留访客的死规定，对有海外家人来访的学生来说「不现实」。

words.enDefinition: not based on clear or sensible reasoning

examples.en: I know it's irrational, but I still check the stove three times before leaving.
examples.zh: 我知道这么想「不理智」，出门前还是要查三遍炉子。

examples.en: Her fear of escalators looked irrational to us until she described the accident she had seen.
examples.zh: 她怕扶梯，我们都觉得这恐惧「不理智」，直到她说出小时候目睹的事故。

words.enDefinition: so unreasonable that it seems silly

examples.en: Charging each roommate a full utility share is absurd when only one of us stays home.
examples.zh: 只有一人在住，却让每个室友全额分摊水电，简直「荒唐」。

examples.en: It felt absurd to write ten pages about a two-page poem, but everyone survived.
examples.zh: 为两页的诗写十页评论听着「荒唐」，但大家还是熬过来了。

words.enDefinition: very strange and hard to explain

examples.en: We found a bizarre collection of traffic cones stacked in our rental basement.
examples.zh: 我们在出租屋地下室发现一堆「怪异」的交通锥。

examples.en: The most bizarre part of orientation was the team-building chant nobody understood.
examples.zh: 迎新周最「离奇」的环节，是那句没人听得懂的团建口号。

words.enDefinition: unusual, often in a way you distrust

examples.en: There was a peculiar smell in the hallway, so we reported it to the front desk.
examples.zh: 走廊里有股「怪异」的气味，我们报给了前台。

examples.en: He has a peculiar habit of sorting his notes by color before every single exam.
examples.zh: 他有个「古怪」的习惯，每场考试前都按颜色整理笔记。

words.enDefinition: strange in a frightening, unpleasant way

examples.en: The abandoned house at the end of our street looks creepy after dark.
examples.zh: 天黑之后，街尾那栋空屋看着就「令人发毛」。

examples.en: Getting friend requests from forty anonymous accounts felt creepy, so I blocked them all.
examples.zh: 一下子冒出四十个匿名好友申请，真「令人发毛」，我全拉黑了。

words.enDefinition: able to be prevented with care or planning

examples.en: Most freshman mistakes, like skipping orientation week, are completely avoidable with planning.
examples.zh: 像翘掉迎新周这种新生失误，稍微规划一下就「完全可避免」。

examples.en: Her library late fee was avoidable because renewing books online takes thirty seconds.
examples.zh: 她那笔图书馆滞纳金本「可以避免」，网上续借只要三十秒。

words.enDefinition: too painful, difficult, or annoying to accept

examples.en: The heat in our un-air-conditioned dorm was unbearable, so we studied at the cafe.
examples.zh: 没空调的宿舍热得「难以忍受」，我们只能去咖啡馆自习。

examples.en: The wait at the visa office became unbearable without headphones or a good book.
examples.zh: 签证办公室的等待，没耳机没书简直「熬不住」。

words.enDefinition: deserving blame and a feeling of shame

examples.en: Dropping litter right beside the recycling bins is honestly shameful behavior.
examples.zh: 就在回收桶旁边乱扔垃圾，这种行为说真的挺「可耻」。

examples.en: It's shameful when group members take credit for slides they never even opened.
examples.zh: 组员抢走自己连开都没开过的幻灯片的功劳，实在「可耻」。

words.enDefinition: very great in amount or effect and hard to handle

examples.en: The first week's reading list felt overwhelming, so my study group split the chapters.
examples.zh: 第一周的阅读清单「多得吓人」，我们学习小组就分章认领了。

examples.en: The international office gave us overwhelming support—campus tours, SIM cards, even a welcome lunch.
examples.zh: 国际学生办公室的支持「铺天盖地」：校园导览、电话卡，还有欢迎午餐。

words.enDefinition: making you feel extremely sad

examples.en: It was heartbreaking to watch the flood volunteers sort through damaged family photos.
examples.zh: 看洪灾志愿者整理泡坏的家庭照片，真让人「心碎」。

examples.en: The documentary about separated families ends with a heartbreaking scene at the airport.
examples.zh: 那部讲离散家庭的纪录片，结尾机场一幕「令人心碎」。

words.enDefinition: involving terrible sadness, often death or disaster

examples.en: Local news covered the tragic highway crash near campus for the entire week.
examples.zh: 本地新闻整整一周都在报道校园附近那起「悲惨的」高速车祸。

examples.en: His grandfather's tragic journey across the war zone made the seminar go quiet.
examples.zh: 他祖父穿越战区的「悲惨」经历让整个研讨课安静下来。

words.enDefinition: causing huge damage or a huge shock

examples.en: The storm had a devastating effect on the small coastal towns along the shore.
examples.zh: 那场风暴对沿岸小镇造成了「毁灭性」的打击。

examples.en: Losing her scholarship right before the semester started was devastating news for her.
examples.zh: 开学前夕失去奖学金，这个消息对她是「毁灭性」的打击。

words.enDefinition: making you worried, upset, or alarmed

examples.en: The documentary showed disturbing images of plastic waste washing up on beaches.
examples.zh: 纪录片里海滩上塑料垃圾的画面「令人不安」。

examples.en: It was disturbing to see how fast the rumor spread through the class group chat.
examples.zh: 谣言在班级群里传得那么快，看着真「让人不安」。

words.enDefinition: giving people energy and hope to act

examples.en: Our guest speaker's journey from a refugee camp to becoming an engineer was genuinely inspiring.
examples.zh: 嘉宾演讲者从难民营走进工程师行业的经历实在「激励人心」。

examples.en: She found the alumni panel so inspiring that she applied for the same fellowship.
examples.zh: 那场校友分享太「鼓舞人心」了，她当场申请了同一个奖学金项目。

words.enDefinition: making you feel happier and more hopeful

examples.en: The choir's graduation performance was so uplifting that the whole crowd stood up.
examples.zh: 合唱团的毕业演出「振奋人心」，全场都起立了。

examples.en: I keep an uplifting playlist for slow mornings when I need a mood boost.
examples.zh: 状态低迷的早晨，我靠一张「振奋人心」的歌单打气。

words.enDefinition: causing tender, sympathetic feelings

examples.en: His touching farewell note to the dorm staff made a couple of RAs tear up.
examples.zh: 他写给宿舍管理员的「动人」告别便条让两位宿管红了眼眶。

examples.en: It was a touching moment when the whole class signed a card for our recovering professor.
examples.zh: 全班为康复中的教授签名写贺卡，那一刻十分「动人」。

words.enDefinition: extremely interesting and holding your full attention

examples.en: The museum's exhibit of ancient sea maps was fascinating—I stayed two extra hours.
examples.zh: 博物馆的古海图展「太吸引人」了，我多待了两个小时。

examples.en: My linguistics professor makes regional accents absolutely fascinating to study and compare.
examples.zh: 语言学教授把各地口音讲得「引人入胜」，比较起来特别有意思。

words.enDefinition: interesting because mysterious or unusual

examples.en: The intriguing flyer with no club name made half the quad scan the QR code.
examples.zh: 那张不署社团名的传单十分「引人好奇」，半个广场的人都扫了码。

examples.en: Her intriguing question about dreams kept the psychology seminar talking well past noon.
examples.zh: 她关于梦的「耐人寻味」的提问，让心理学研讨课讨论过了午。

words.enDefinition: fun and enjoyable to watch or hear

examples.en: The campus improv show was entertaining enough that we forgot our midterm stress.
examples.zh: 校园即兴喜剧「好看又解压」，看完中期考试的焦虑都忘了。

examples.en: My uncle remains the most entertaining storyteller at every family dinner table.
examples.zh: 叔叔一直是家庭餐桌上最「有趣」的讲故事高手。

words.enDefinition: extremely funny

examples.en: Our group chat filled with hilarious memes during the worst week of exams.
examples.zh: 考试最难熬的那周，群聊里全是「爆笑」的表情包。

examples.en: The comedian's impression of our campus security guard was absolutely hilarious.
examples.zh: 那位喜剧演员模仿我们学校保安，实在「太好笑」了。

words.enDefinition: over-sentimental in an embarrassing, overused way

examples.en: The pickup lines at the welcome party were so cheesy that everyone burst out laughing.
examples.zh: 迎新派对上的搭讪台词「土味十足」，所有人笑作一团。

examples.en: I love that cheesy holiday movie even though the plot is completely predictable.
examples.zh: 那部情节「老套」的节日电影我照样百看不厌。

words.enDefinition: easy to remember and repeat, like a tune

examples.en: That convenience store jingle is so catchy that I hum it in the shower.
examples.zh: 便利店的广告曲特别「洗脑」，我洗澡都会哼。

examples.en: Our club finally wrote a catchy slogan that freshmen started repeating within a week.
examples.zh: 社团终于想出一句「朗朗上口」的口号，一周内新生都会念了。

words.enDefinition: easy to foresee exactly what will happen

examples.en: The plot was predictable, but we still enjoyed the film's gorgeous soundtrack.
examples.zh: 剧情「毫无悬念」，但电影的配乐我们依然喜欢。

examples.en: His late replies became so predictable that she stopped waiting by her phone.
examples.zh: 他的回复总是「迟得可以预见」，她干脆不等手机了。

words.enDefinition: easy to connect with from your own life

examples.en: Her blog about first-year visa struggles is relatable for almost every international student.
examples.zh: 她写的第一年签证波折博客，几乎每个留学生都「有共鸣」。

examples.en: The speaker shared relatable stories about failing his driving test three straight times.
examples.zh: 演讲者连挂三次驾照考试的经历让大家特别「有代入感」。

words.enDefinition: so exciting you cannot stop watching or reading

examples.en: The mystery novel was so gripping that I finished it before my Saturday shift.
examples.zh: 那本悬疑小说「扣人心弦」，周六上班前我就读完了。

examples.en: His gripping account of the mountain rescue kept the entire lecture hall silent.
examples.zh: 他讲述的山间救援「惊心动魄」，整个阶梯教室鸦雀无声。

words.enDefinition: full of exciting, fast-moving events

examples.en: We spent Friday night watching an action-packed superhero movie at the discount theater.
examples.zh: 周五晚上我们在廉价影院看了部「紧张刺激」的超级英雄片。

examples.en: Our orientation weekend was action-packed, from the morning campus run to the late bonfire.
examples.zh: 迎新周末行程「满满当当」，从清晨环校跑到深夜篝火。

words.enDefinition: moving, changing, or happening very quickly

examples.en: It took a full month to adjust to the fast-paced schedule of medical school.
examples.zh: 足足一个月我才适应医学院「快节奏」的课表。

examples.en: The fast-paced city exhausted her at first, but now she loves the energy.
examples.zh: 这座「快节奏」的城市起初让她筋疲力尽，如今她爱上了这份活力。

words.enDefinition: written clearly, skillfully, and effectively

examples.en: Her well-written personal statement stood out among hundreds of scholarship applications.
examples.zh: 她那份「写得漂亮」的个人陈述在几百份奖学金申请中脱颖而出。

examples.en: The textbook is well-written, with worked examples that actually make sense to beginners.
examples.zh: 这本教材「写得很好」，例题讲解让初学者真能看懂。

words.enDefinition: so good that you really should not miss it

examples.en: That rooftop light show is a must-see before it ends next month.
examples.zh: 那场天台灯光秀下月收官，是「必看」节目。

examples.en: Her campus guide lists must-see neighborhoods that most tourists usually miss.
examples.zh: 她的攻略列出了游客通常错过的「必去」街区。

words.enDefinition: suitable for adults and children together

examples.en: We picked a family-friendly restaurant so my little cousin could join our dinner.
examples.zh: 我们挑了家「老少皆宜」的餐厅，好让小表妹也来聚餐。

examples.en: The campus movie night stays family-friendly, so nothing too scary ever gets screened.
examples.zh: 校园电影之夜走「合家欢」路线，从来不放太吓人的片子。

words.enDefinition: not interesting in any way

examples.en: The 8 a.m. statistics lecture is so boring that half the class quietly dozes off.
examples.zh: 早上八点的统计课「无聊」到一半人悄悄睡着。

examples.en: Waiting two hours at the DMV with no phone signal was beyond boring.
examples.zh: 在车管所等两个小时还没手机信号，「无聊」到家了。

words.enDefinition: important enough to bring up briefly

examples.en: One detail worth mentioning: the shared dorm kitchens close for cleaning every Sunday night.
examples.zh: 有个细节「值得一提」：宿舍公用厨房每周日晚封闭打扫。

examples.en: It's worth mentioning that the professor accepts late submissions once per term.
examples.zh: 还「值得一提」的是，教授每学期允许迟交一次作业。

words.enDefinition: fashionable in a simple, elegant way

examples.en: Her chic thrifted blazer looked like it came straight from a boutique downtown.
examples.zh: 她那件二手店淘来的外套「雅致时髦」，像市中心精品店的货。

examples.en: The new cafe near campus has a chic minimalist design with plants everywhere.
examples.zh: 校园旁新开的咖啡馆设计「简约别致」，到处摆着绿植。

words.enDefinition: stylish and high quality in a neat way

examples.en: He wore a classy navy suit to the career fair, and recruiters noticed immediately.
examples.zh: 他穿「有格调」的深蓝西装去招聘会，招聘官立刻注意到他。

examples.en: The hotel lobby feels classy even though their lunch menu is student-budget friendly.
examples.zh: 酒店大堂十分「有格调」，午餐菜单却很对学生钱包友好。

words.enDefinition: loudly impressive in order to attract attention

examples.en: He parked his flashy sports car outside the library, which felt odd for a TA.
examples.zh: 他把「浮夸」的跑车停在图书馆外，助教开这车有点怪。

examples.en: I skip flashy phone cases and choose plain ones that actually survive drops.
examples.zh: 我不买「花里胡哨」的手机壳，只挑耐摔的素款。

words.enDefinition: currently fashionable and popular

examples.en: That trendy boba shop opened two blocks from our dorm last weekend.
examples.zh: 那家「新潮」的奶茶店上周末开到了宿舍两条街外。

examples.en: Thrift stores are trendy again because students want style on a part-time budget.
examples.zh: 二手店又「时髦」回来了，学生党想靠兼职预算穿出风格。

words.enDefinition: belonging to an older style, not modern

examples.en: My grandmother still keeps an old-fashioned paper calendar instead of any phone app.
examples.zh: 我奶奶还在用「老式」纸质日历，不用任何手机应用。

examples.en: The diner kept its old-fashioned stools and chrome counters from the 1950s.
examples.zh: 这家餐馆保留着上世纪五十年代「老式」的吧台凳和铬合金柜台。

words.enDefinition: not dated by fashion or passing time

examples.en: That little black dress is timeless—my mother has worn hers for twenty years.
examples.zh: 那条小黑裙「永不过时」，我妈妈的一条穿了二十年。

examples.en: The professor says Shakespeare stays timeless because its emotions never age.
examples.zh: 教授说莎士比亚「历久弥新」，因为其中的情感从不过时。

words.enDefinition: loose-fitting and hanging away from the body

examples.en: I wear baggy sweatshirts to my 8 a.m. labs when I don't want to think about outfits.
examples.zh: 早上八点有实验课又不想搭配衣服时，我就套件「宽松」的卫衣出门。

examples.en: These jeans were baggy a month ago, so my gym plan is clearly working.
examples.zh: 这条牛仔裤一个月前还「松垮」的，看来健身计划见效了。

words.enDefinition: very thin, often more than is healthy

examples.en: My cousin got skinny over summer training with his university track team.
examples.zh: 表哥随校田径队训练了一个暑假，整个人变得「精瘦」。

examples.en: He looked skinny after a semester of instant noodles, so we started cooking together.
examples.zh: 吃了一学期泡面他「瘦得脱相」，我们就开始一起做饭了。

words.enDefinition: untidy and uncared for in appearance

examples.en: He looked scruffy after finals week—three-day stubble and a wrinkled hoodie.
examples.zh: 期末周过后他「邋里邋遢」，三天没刮的胡子和皱卫衣。

examples.en: The scruffy puppy at the shelter turned out to be the friendliest one there.
examples.zh: 收容所里那只「邋遢」的小狗其实是最亲人的。

words.enDefinition: wearing neat, attractive, suitable clothes

examples.en: The well-dressed recruiter somehow remembered every candidate's name at the crowded booth.
examples.zh: 那位「衣着得体」的招聘官竟记住了展位上每位候选人的名字。

examples.en: He arrived well-dressed for the video interview even though only his top half showed.
examples.zh: 视频面试只拍上半身，他还是「穿着讲究」地出了镜。

words.enDefinition: very beautiful and delightful to look at

examples.en: The botanical garden looks gorgeous when the cherry trees bloom in early April.
examples.zh: 四月初樱花盛开时，植物园「美极了」。

examples.en: She took a gorgeous photo of our study group by the lake at sunset.
examples.zh: 日落时她在湖边给我们学习小组拍了张「超美」的照片。

words.enDefinition: extremely ugly or offensive to look at

examples.en: The landlord painted our hallway a hideous green that nobody can quite explain.
examples.zh: 房东把楼道刷成了「丑得离谱」的绿色，没人说得清为什么。

examples.en: Those hideous 3D-printed trophies still made the whole club burst out laughing.
examples.zh: 那些「丑陋」的3D打印奖杯反倒让全社笑成一团。

words.enDefinition: cute in a way that makes you feel affection

examples.en: The neighbor's golden retriever puppy is adorable, so I volunteer to walk it.
examples.zh: 邻居家的金毛幼犬「可爱」极了，我主动帮忙遛狗。

examples.en: Her adorable hand-knitted mittens became the most requested gift that whole winter.
examples.zh: 她那双「可爱」的手织手套成了那年冬天最受欢迎的礼物。

words.enDefinition: showing good judgment of style and beauty

examples.en: They decorated the tiny studio with tasteful string lights and two framed prints.
examples.zh: 他们用「雅致」的串灯和两幅装裱画装点了小公寓。

examples.en: Her tasteful thank-you card made the host family feel appreciated for months.
examples.zh: 她那张「有品位」的感谢卡让寄宿家庭感动了好几个月。

words.enDefinition: worn out and looking poor in condition

examples.en: The once-shabby guesthouse was renovated last year and now hosts exchange students.
examples.zh: 那家曾经「破旧」的小旅馆去年翻新，现在接待交换生。

examples.en: He keeps his shabby old sneakers for the gym even after buying new ones.
examples.zh: 买了新鞋之后，他还是穿着那双「破旧」的旧鞋去健身房。

words.enDefinition: done carelessly and without attention to detail

examples.en: The TA marked my lab report down for sloppy units and missing labels.
examples.zh: 助教因我实验报告单位「马虎」、标签缺失而扣了分。

examples.en: His sloppy handwriting cost him real points because the grader couldn't read the proofs.
examples.zh: 他字迹「潦草」，阅卷老师看不清证明过程，实打实丢了分。

words.enDefinition: requiring a lot of time, skill, or effort

examples.en: My organic chemistry course is demanding, so I block two library hours every evening.
examples.zh: 有机化学课「要求很高」，我每晚固定两小时泡图书馆。

examples.en: The demanding internship taught her more in three months than a year of lectures.
examples.zh: 那段「高强度」的实习三个月教她的东西比一年听课还多。

words.enDefinition: done so skillfully it looks easy

examples.en: Her effortless presentation came from rehearsing those same slides fifteen times.
examples.zh: 她的展示「轻松自如」，秘诀是把同样的幻灯片排练了十五遍。

examples.en: He made the lake swim look effortless, then admitted he was completely exhausted.
examples.zh: 他游过湖面显得「毫不费力」，上岸却承认累坏了。

words.enDefinition: causing no pain, trouble, or difficulty

examples.en: The online tax form was surprisingly painless once I gathered all my documents.
examples.zh: 备齐材料后，线上报税表填起来出乎意料地「轻松省事」。

examples.en: The dentist promised a painless filling, and for once she kept her word.
examples.zh: 牙医承诺补牙「不会疼」，这次她还真说到做到。

words.enDefinition: long and slow in a boring way

examples.en: Copying citations by hand is tedious, so I finally learned a reference manager.
examples.zh: 手抄参考文献太「枯燥繁琐」，我终于学会了文献管理软件。

examples.en: Data entry for the survey was tedious, but it covered my textbook budget.
examples.zh: 问卷数据录入虽「单调乏味」，却够我买这学期的教材。

words.enDefinition: awkward and complicated to do or use

examples.en: The scholarship application was so cumbersome that half of our cohort gave up halfway.
examples.zh: 奖学金申请流程「繁琐至极」，我们这届一半人半途放弃。

examples.en: Renting textbooks used to be cumbersome until the library added an online request form.
examples.zh: 以前租教材手续「麻烦」，图书馆上线申请表单后就好办多了。

words.enDefinition: done with extremely careful attention to detail

examples.en: Her painstaking lecture notes saved the whole study group before the comprehensive exam.
examples.zh: 通识大考前，她「一丝不苟」的课堂笔记救了整个学习小组。

examples.en: Restoring the old campus mural took painstaking work from the art department volunteers.
examples.zh: 修复老校园壁画是件「费尽心思」的活儿，全靠艺术系志愿者。

words.enDefinition: difficult in a way that tests your ability

examples.en: The advanced statistics course is challenging, but the TA's office hours help enormously.
examples.zh: 高阶统计课「很有挑战」，不过助教答疑时间帮了大忙。

examples.en: Volunteering with a class of toddlers was challenging and tripled her patience.
examples.zh: 给一屋子学步小孩做志愿教学很「考验人」，她的耐心翻了三倍。

words.enDefinition: needing care or skill because easily got wrong

examples.en: The parallel parking section of my driving test was tricky, but I passed anyway.
examples.zh: 路考的侧方停车环节很「难缠」，好在我还是过了。

examples.en: Splitting the security deposit three ways got tricky when one roommate left early.
examples.zh: 一位室友提前搬走后，三个人怎么分押金就「不好办」了。

words.enDefinition: full of small detailed connected parts

examples.en: The intricate dance routine took our culture club three months to perfect.
examples.zh: 那套「繁复」的舞蹈动作我们文化社练了三个月才齐。

examples.en: She loves intricate puzzles, so the two-thousand-piece jigsaw was a perfect birthday gift.
examples.zh: 她痴迷「复杂精细」的拼图，两千块的拼图正是完美生日礼物。

words.enDefinition: extremely tiring and lasting a long time

examples.en: The three-hour placement exam was grueling, but my practice tests paid off.
examples.zh: 三小时的分级考试「磨人」得很，好在刷题没有白费。

examples.en: Orientation week was grueling—campus tours under the summer sun from nine to five.
examples.zh: 迎新周「累得够呛」：顶着烈日从早九参观到晚五。

words.enDefinition: impossible to understand or explain

examples.en: The dorm's mail sorting system is baffling—my packages keep ending up three doors away.
examples.zh: 宿舍的分拣系统「让人摸不着头脑」，我的包裹总跑到三间房外。

examples.en: His baffling absence from the final turned out to be a family emergency.
examples.zh: 他期末考试的「神秘」缺席原来是家里出了急事。

words.enDefinition: using more money, time, or things than needed

examples.en: Ordering takeout every night turned out wasteful, so our floor started a cooking rota.
examples.zh: 每晚点外卖其实很「浪费」，我们一层楼搞起了轮值做饭。

examples.en: Leaving the heater on all day is wasteful when the timer switch costs nothing.
examples.zh: 暖气全天开着实在「浪费」，定时开关又不花钱。

words.enDefinition: achieving a lot within the time available

examples.en: Early mornings at the quiet cafe are my most productive study hours.
examples.zh: 清晨安静的咖啡馆是我学习「效率最高」的时段。

examples.en: It was a productive meeting—we assigned every task and set real deadlines.
examples.zh: 这场会议「卓有成效」：每项任务都分派到人，还定了真正的截止日。

words.enDefinition: wasting time or energy while working

examples.en: Printing a handout for everyone felt inefficient, so our seminar switched to shared PDFs.
examples.zh: 给每人打印讲义「效率太低」，研讨课改用共享PDF了。

examples.en: The cafeteria's two-cashier setup is inefficient during the noon rush, so lines crawl.
examples.zh: 午高峰时食堂只开两个收银台「效率低」，队伍挪得像蜗牛。

words.enDefinition: not sensible or convenient to actually use

examples.en: Lugging my desktop computer to the dorm was impractical, so I switched to a laptop.
examples.zh: 把台式机搬进宿舍「不实用」，我后来换成了笔记本。

examples.en: Carrying six textbooks across campus every day is impractical, so I photograph the chapters instead.
examples.zh: 每天背六本教材穿校园「不实用」，我改拍章节照片了。

words.enDefinition: possible to do with available resources

examples.en: Graduating a semester early is feasible if I take two summer courses online.
examples.zh: 只要修两门暑期网课，提前一学期毕业是「可行」的。

examples.en: The committee questioned whether the rooftop garden was feasible within this year's budget.
examples.zh: 委员会质疑按今年预算建天台花园是否「行得通」。

words.enDefinition: possible to reach with reasonable effort

examples.en: Saving fifty dollars a month is an achievable goal even on my part-time wage.
examples.zh: 就算靠兼职工资，每月存五十美元也是个「能实现」的目标。

examples.en: The coach set achievable weekly targets so the beginner swimmers stayed motivated.
examples.zh: 教练给新手定「够得着」的周目标，让大家保持干劲。

words.enDefinition: useful for many different purposes

examples.en: A versatile denim jacket works for class, part-time shifts, and weekend hikes.
examples.zh: 一件「百搭」的牛仔外套上课、兼职、周末徒步都能穿。

examples.en: Eggs are so versatile—fried rice, omelets, or a quick ramen upgrade at midnight.
examples.zh: 鸡蛋「用途超广」：蛋炒饭、煎蛋，或深夜给泡面升级。

words.enDefinition: regular, continuous, and not changing suddenly

examples.en: A steady weekend job at the campus bookstore covers my phone bill and coffee.
examples.zh: 校书店一份「稳定」的周末工作够我付话费和咖啡钱。

examples.en: His steady progress in speaking came from practicing with the language partner program daily.
examples.zh: 他口语「稳步」进步，靠的是每天参加语伴项目练习。

words.enDefinition: fixed and strict, unwilling to bend or change

examples.en: The professor was rigid about deadlines until a student explained her visa-related delays.
examples.zh: 教授对截止日期一向「死板」，直到有学生解释了签证带来的延误。

examples.en: Our rigid chore schedule fell apart during finals, so we switched to a shared app.
examples.zh: 期末周「僵化」的值日表垮了，我们换成了共享应用。

words.enDefinition: not clearly expressed or specific

examples.en: Her vague directions to the pickup point had me circling the science building for twenty minutes.
examples.zh: 她给的取货地点「含糊不清」，我绕着理科楼转了二十分钟。

examples.en: The syllabus was vague about grading, so I emailed the TA for the exact rubric.
examples.zh: 教学大纲对评分「说得含糊」，我发邮件向助教要了评分细则。

words.enDefinition: open to more than one meaning or reading

examples.en: One ambiguous clause in our lease caused a two-week argument over the deposit.
examples.zh: 租约里一条「模棱两可」的条款引发了两周的押金争执。

examples.en: His ambiguous reply—'maybe, we'll see'—left everyone unsure about the road trip.
examples.zh: 他那句"再说吧"的回复「含糊其辞」，大家都不确定自驾游还去不去。

words.enDefinition: real and sincere, not pretended

examples.en: My host family's genuine interest in my hometown made every dinner conversation easy.
examples.zh: 寄宿家庭对我家乡「真心」的好奇让每顿晚餐都聊得轻松。

examples.en: He offered a genuine apology and replaced the speaker he borrowed without being asked.
examples.zh: 他「诚恳地」道了歉，没等人催就赔了借坏的音箱。

words.enDefinition: true to its origin and not copied

examples.en: That family-run dumpling house two blocks away serves the most authentic food near campus.
examples.zh: 离校园两个街区的那家家庭饺子馆最「正宗」。

examples.en: Her authentic tamales came from her grandmother's handwritten recipe notebook, not any website.
examples.zh: 她的「地道」玉米粽配方来自祖母的手写笔记，不是网上抄的。

words.enDefinition: not real although made to look real

examples.en: Campus security warned us about fake parking ticket emails going around this week.
examples.zh: 校警提醒大家，本周流传着「假的」停车罚单邮件。

examples.en: That 'leather' jacket from the night market fell apart in a month—totally fake.
examples.zh: 夜市买的"皮"夹克一个月就散架——纯属「假货」。

words.enDefinition: made by people rather than occurring naturally

examples.en: Our dorm's artificial Christmas tree saves us from vacuuming needles every single day.
examples.zh: 宿舍的「人造」圣诞树让我们免于每天吸松针。

examples.en: She avoids artificial sweeteners and just uses half a spoon of real sugar.
examples.zh: 她不碰「人工」甜味剂，宁可放半勺真糖。

words.enDefinition: only on the surface, without depth

examples.en: Their superficial small talk never got beyond weather, majors, and weekend plans.
examples.zh: 他们的闲聊「浮于表面」，话题从没超出天气、专业和周末安排。

examples.en: The draft gave a superficial overview of the issue without citing a single study.
examples.zh: 初稿对问题的梳理「很肤浅」，一项研究都没引用。

words.enDefinition: advanced, complex, and refined in design

examples.en: The library's sophisticated room-booking app even suggests free study spaces near you.
examples.zh: 图书馆「精密」的订座应用还会推荐附近的空位。

examples.en: His surprisingly sophisticated espresso setup makes our tiny shared kitchen feel like a cafe.
examples.zh: 他那套「精良」的意式咖啡设备让我们的小厨房像家咖啡馆。

words.enDefinition: introducing new ideas and better methods

examples.en: Our engineering club built an innovative bike-route map that freshmen actually use.
examples.zh: 我们工程社做了一张「有创意」的骑行路线图，新生真的在用。

examples.en: The professor rewarded innovative approaches even when the final prototype failed completely.
examples.zh: 即使原型机彻底失败，教授也奖励「创新」的思路。

words.enDefinition: at the most advanced stage of development

examples.en: The robotics lab receives cutting-edge equipment that most undergraduate courses never touch.
examples.zh: 机器人实验室配「尖端」设备，多数本科课程根本碰不到。

examples.en: Her cutting-edge research on battery recycling won this year's undergraduate poster prize.
examples.zh: 她那项电池回收的「前沿」研究拿下了今年的本科生海报奖。

words.enDefinition: more than is reasonable, needed, or allowed

examples.en: The landlord charged an excessive fee for one tiny nail hole in the wall.
examples.zh: 墙上就一个钉子眼，房东却收了笔「过高」的费用。

examples.en: The doctor blamed my excessive screen time for the headaches and told me to cut back.
examples.zh: 医生说我持续的头痛源于「过度」刷屏，让我少看点。

words.enDefinition: not enough for the purpose or need

examples.en: My first loan offer was insufficient, so I added weekend tutoring to close the gap.
examples.zh: 首笔贷款「不够用」，我就加了周末家教来补缺口。

examples.en: The doctor said my insufficient sleep was behind the constant afternoon headaches.
examples.zh: 医生说我下午的持续头痛源于睡眠「不足」。

words.enDefinition: not connected to the matter being discussed

examples.en: The interviewer gently cut my story short because those details were irrelevant to the role.
examples.zh: 那些细节和岗位「无关」，面试官温和地打断了我的故事。

examples.en: Skipping irrelevant sources early keeps your literature review focused and your deadlines safe.
examples.zh: 早点剔除「不相干」的文献，综述才能聚焦、截止日才保得住。

words.enDefinition: of very little importance or value

examples.en: Don't spend your whole weekend on trivial formatting—outline the main argument first.
examples.zh: 别把整个周末耗在「琐碎」的排版上，先列出核心论点。

examples.en: The building manager dismissed our trivial complaints but finally fixed the heating.
examples.zh: 楼管把我们的「鸡毛蒜皮」晾在一边，总算修了暖气。

words.enDefinition: extreme and sudden in effect or change

examples.en: Rent jumped so sharply that we made the drastic decision to move farther out.
examples.zh: 房租涨幅「急剧」，我们只好狠下心搬远些。

examples.en: The doctor warned me against drastic diets and suggested steady, regular meals instead.
examples.zh: 医生警告我别搞「极端」节食，建议三餐规律、循序渐进。
